title: V4 Guards 1.2.x onboarding Profile authoring and UI-first repair
goal: Repair installed onboarding, add supported non-authoritative Profile candidate authoring and a UI-first human flow, correctly interpret simple inherited .NET frameworks, and prove zero persistent environment mutation while retaining Host and human authority boundaries.
acceptanceCriteria: The single public installed launcher runs version, profile discover and a new Profile draft without wrapper-parameter tricks or requiring the new Profile to already exist.

Launcher arguments preserve ordered strings, nested entrypoints cannot derive duplicated paths, and failures have stable capturable categories and exit codes under both supported PowerShell invocation styles.
Profile configure validates a separate candidate and atomically creates a deterministic StateRoot-owned configured Draft without changing the original Draft or discovery evidence.
Profile review-template creates a deterministic incomplete document that cannot validate or promote as an accepted human review.
Architecture configuration requires non-empty enabledClaims selected by Profile rules and rejects stale, tampered, unsupported or capability-exceeding inputs.
A simple literal TargetFramework inherited from Directory.Build.props is evidenced correctly while conditional, imported, expression-based or ambiguous values remain unsupported coverage.
Web Companion provides a typed UI-first onboarding stepper from verified installation through configured candidate and incomplete review template with at most one shell start command.
Browser operations use Host-derived identifiers and cannot supply raw paths, Host arguments, shell text, environment values, Target writes, activation, remote changes or human acceptance.
Static and dynamic regressions prove install, launcher, isolated dotnet child processes and cleanup do not modify persisted User or Machine environment variables, PATH or PowerShell profiles.
A local candidate uses one consistent unused 1.2 patch version and passes focused, CLI, package and Web Companion tests without publishing or changing a consumer repository.
risks: A convenience flow could accidentally turn non-authoritative discovery or recommendations into accepted policy.
Browser-controlled paths or commands could bypass the Host authority and filesystem boundary.
Prerequisite simplification could skip required Module runtimes for executable stage operations.
Partial MSBuild interpretation could misclassify unsupported inherited framework expressions as violations.
A test or installer could copy process PATH into persistent User or Machine PATH and destabilize the host.
A 1.2.x candidate could be mistaken for publication or consumer protection authorization.
decisions: Use profile configure and profile review-template as the supported authoring command names.
Keep Drafts, configured candidates and incomplete review templates non-authoritative and StateRoot-owned.
Permit only typed preview-bound stale-refusing StateRoot writes from Web Companion and forbid Target, CI, activation, remote and human-acceptance writes.
Keep CLI and Web Companion on the same Host contracts, with Web Companion as the primary human onboarding path.
Interpret only simple unconditional literal central target-framework declarations and classify all richer MSBuild forms as unsupported coverage.
Treat persisted environment data and PowerShell profiles as immutable host-owned state and stop on any drift.
Target the 1.2.x patch line, resolve one unused exact patch version before candidate creation and require a separate Plan for publication or IFX retesting.
